wireDescriptor.description: Attach an agent-authored annotation to a symbol in the shared index. Provenance is enforced: the row records author class 'agent' (never spoofable), the calling tool identity, and timestamps. Re-annotating the same symbol+path updates the note in place — one note per author per location, enforced by a unique index over (project, symbol, author, path). The symbol is NOT checked against the index, so a note may name anything; instead the reply MEASURES whether an editor surface can show it and says so in `surfacing` (`editor`, `matchedAs`, `matchedNames`, `statement`) — a typo'd name or a qualified name is stored and reported honestly rather than promised to a surface it cannot reach. `path` is resolved to the index's own spelling, so `src/a.ts`, `./src/a.ts` and the absolute path are the same note. Annotations are opinions layered on evidence, never index facts. To change source code use bb_edit; to read notes back use bb_annotations.

symbol.description: symbol name to annotate (`target`/`query` are accepted as aliases)

path.description: optional file path to disambiguate same-named symbols; resolved to the index's own spelling (`brain_file.relative_path`), so `src/a.ts`, `./src/a.ts` and the absolute path all reach the same note

toolIdentity.description: optional name of the calling agent/tool (recorded verbatim)

defects.title: `surfacing.editor` can be true when the name and the path match DIFFERENT files, and the reply then promises a render that never happens
defects.detail: annotationReachability() measures name reachability (name/qualified_name anywhere in the project) and canonicalFilePath() measures path reachability (any indexed file). The handler ANDs the two booleans. A note on `greet` with path `other.ts` — where `other.ts` is indexed but does not declare `greet` — is reported editor:true with the statement "renders in the editor hover section and graph badge", while hover(main.ts:greet) and the bb/graph root both show nothing. Measured through the real MCP door.
defects.fix: handler measures the JOINT predicate: when a path is given and resolves, at least one symbol carrying the name/qualified name must be declared in THAT file, or editor:false with a statement naming the file

defects.title: the tool's own gate suite never exercises the real MCP door
defects.detail: verify-annotation-store.ts calls createToolHandlers() directly, bypassing validateToolArguments, the per-mode index gate, and the wire error envelope. The real door answers differently for some inputs: a missing symbol is 'error: bb_annotate: missing required option: symbol', and an author_class/authorClass spoof is REFUSED as an unknown option, whereas the gate's direct call asserts a successful write with provenance 'agent'. The provenance conclusion is right; the wire contract it claims is not what the gate measured.
defects.evidence: PHASE-A-PROBES.json phases.refusals (labels 'missing symbol', 'author_class spoof') vs script/m28/verify-annotation-store.ts R2
defects.fix: Phase B adds a real `bb mcp` stdio session leg to A1 (success + refusals captured from the wire)

defects.title: A1's 'mutation suite' mutants are mostly not planted defects
defects.detail: M2/M3 are positive checks over strings (a manual SQL corruption and a literal slice); they re-assert the round trip rather than planting a defect in the tool and requiring the suite to notice. Only M1 mutates storage (a NULL author_class insert), which proves the schema trigger, not the handler. A handler regression that derived author_class from arguments, ignored the path in the location key, or always claimed reachability would not be caught by M2–M4.
defects.evidence: script/m28/verify-annotation-store.ts lines 144-202; mutant labels vs their bodies
defects.fix: Phase B plants real handler mutants beside the module (same mechanism as verify-mcp-tools.ts) and requires the suite to go red

defects.title: docs claims that are not true today (reachability AND-claim, 'constant-time', milestone narration, missing guide page)
defects.detail: docs/tools/bb_annotate.md and the curation source say editor is the AND of nameMatched/pathMatched (falsified by PA-1), call the write 'constant-time' (unmeasured), carry the limitation 'Annotation store semantics are owned by the M28 workstream' (§9 milestone narration, no measurable content), and do not state that the first write on an unindexed project creates that project's annotation store. The handler and curation headers point at a docs/BB_*.md guide page for annotations that does not exist.
defects.evidence: docs/tools/bb_annotate.md:54,72,82; curation lines; list of docs/BB_*.md contains no annotation guide
defects.fix: Phase B rewrites the curation text from measurements (LATENCY.json), adds the joint-reachability and unindexed-store statements, removes the milestone line, and fixes the headers (a guide page is outside this lane's write scope — requested from the Lead)

defects.title: handler regex is frozen debt with no allowlist entry
defects.detail: The control-character check uses /[\u0000-\u001F\u007F]/; a character-code scan is a direct non-regex formulation, so the use fails charter §7's 'genuinely unavoidable' test.
defects.evidence: validation/tools/regex-baseline.json (entry for src/mcp/tools/bb_annotate/handler.ts); regex policy PASS 14 allowlisted / 73 frozen / 0 new
defects.fix: Phase B replaces it with a code-point scan (regex debt decreases, no allowlist row added)

defects.title: input bounds are declared for body and toolIdentity but not for symbol and path
